summary: a file is not JSON the reader can follow, or holds no storage layout in a form the tool reads (a layout object, an artifact with storageLayout, a compiler output with contracts)
fix: Give the storage layout as the compiler, forge inspect or an artifact writes it (docs/inputs.md), and fix the line named.

summary: a variable or a type of a layout lacks what the comparison needs (a label, slot, offset or type, a size, a type that is not in types); that part was not compared
fix: Give the layout as the compiler writes it, or compare that part by hand.

summary: a variable of the old layout is not in the new one, under its name or at its place
fix: Keep the variable at its place, under its old name or a new one; if it is no longer used, leave it declared and unused.

summary: a variable is at another slot or offset in the new layout
fix: Declare the variables in the old order and keep every base contract as it was; add new variables after the last one, or take their slots from a gap.

summary: a variable keeps its name and gets a type with another storage form: another size or signedness, another mapping key or value, other struct members, another array length, or enum members removed or reordered
fix: Keep the old type; add a variable of the new type after the last one and move the data in an upgrade step.

summary: a new variable takes storage that a variable of the old layout used, as happens when it is declared before existing ones or in a base contract with no room
fix: Declare new variables after the last one, or in a base contract take their slots from its gap.

summary: the slots added before a storage gap in a contract are not the slots the gap was cut by, so what follows the gap moves
fix: Cut the gap by exactly the slots the new variables take, counting how they pack.

summary: a contract that had a storage gap has none in the new layout
fix: Keep a gap in every base contract that may grow; drop it only when the variables that replace it take exactly its slots.
own: keeping a gap in every contract that had one is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Solidity or OpenZeppelin documentation; the OpenZeppelin page describes gaps as a convention

summary: the contracts that hold storage come in another order in the new layout
fix: Keep the base contracts in their old order; a new base contract with storage needs room that does not move the others, such as a namespace.

summary: an ERC-7201 namespace of the old layout is not in the new one
fix: Keep the namespace struct with its annotation and its members, even those no longer used.

summary: a variable of the new layout takes a slot that ERC-1967 sets aside for a proxy (the logic contract, the beacon or the admin)
fix: Move the variable, or the base slot of a custom layout, away from the ERC-1967 slots.

summary: a variable of the old layout has a new name, or is declared in another contract, at the same slot and offset with the same storage form, so it keeps the old value
fix: Confirm that the variable means the same as before, since it starts with the old value.

summary: a variable keeps its place and its storage form under another type name: a contract type and address, string and bytes, a renamed struct or enum, a user-defined value type
fix: Confirm that the stored values mean the same under the new type.
own: reading these types as one storage form is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Solidity or OpenZeppelin documentation; it rests on the sizes and encodings in the layout and on the page that says bytes and string are encoded the same way

summary: members were appended to a struct stored as a mapping value or within its old size, or to an enum, and what was stored keeps its place
fix: Confirm that the code handles what was stored before the upgrade: appended struct members read as zero there.
own: accepting appended members is a best practice of this tool, not a rule in the Solidity or OpenZeppelin documentation; it follows from the layout rules for mapping values, which the OpenZeppelin page does not discuss
